name: Failed Quality Gate Stops Pipeline Advancement
text: Gluhak and Pavlič provide direct operational support for Kaal's fail-closed control rule. Their CI/CD case study uses dependent quality checks. If any check fails, the pipeline fails and the code is not integrated into the larger codebase. This independently instantiates a failed control stopping advancement instead of merely annotating a run. The comparison is bounded. The source concerns software-delivery pipelines and static source-code quality, not autonomous-agent reputation infrastructure or Kaal's broader control taxonomy.

sourceEvidencePassages.text: A key to success lies in establishing widely agreed rules, then are enforced in every development iteration. A quality gate in a CI/CD pipeline can be realized in the form of a static source code analysis. It offers a repeatable and a consistent internal quality analysis after every source code push to a version control system.
